source.version_note: Publisher's version of record in a two-cover-page PEARL repository wrapper. Consciousness and Cognition124:103733, available7August2024. PDF metadata creation2026 does not change the printed2024 publication year.

citation.title: Large language models have divergent effects on self-perceptions of mind and the attributes considered uniquely human

reading.source_scope_note: Human pre/post self-report study after viewing three fixed GPT4 prompt-response examples. No measured model psychological mechanism, real-time interaction or unexposed comparison group. Social comparison and psychological distance are discussed theoretical constructs, not experimentally isolated mediators.
access_limits: All8 extracted pages read, including repository wrappers, methods, results, figure captions, limitations and references.

External OSF raw data, full presented ChatGPT examples, cited original comparison/distance studies and individual scatterplot points were not independently retrieved. Graphs are summarized using the article's numerical results rather than estimated visual heights.

study.design: Single-group repeated self-report before and after three fixed ChatGPTGPT4 examples
study.exposure: Nature/nurture, feet-in-shoe question, cover letter for a janitorial position on the Moon
study.measures: Five-item mind survey (2agency,3experience), two single self-ratings and two human-uniqueness items; morality item accidentally omitted

summary: After brief fixed-example exposure, participants reported slightly higher self-attributed agency/experience and lower uniqueness of those qualities to humans. Add social comparison and psychological distance as explicitly secondary theoretical constructs. Neither these shifts nor a human-uniqueness item demonstrates dehumanization, a causal anthropomorphism mediator or actual model experience.

findings.definition: Evaluating one's own abilities, qualities or standing in relation to other people or comparison targets.
findings.novelty_rationale: A relational self-evaluation process distinct from conforming to a majority, seeking validation or preferentially recalling self-relevant information. Comparing oneself with AI is a proposed extension; upward/downward direction is retained within this entry rather than counted as separate mechanisms.

evidence.quote: We define and perceive ourselves often in comparison to others
This sort of downward comparison could explain the elevated self-perception of one’s capabilities.

findings.evidence_scope: The paper invokes Festinger and later reviews to explain pre/post self-rating shifts in133 humans. It does not randomly vary comparison targets, directly measure comparison direction or establish social comparison as a mediator. Original comparison-theory papers not independently read.
findings.boundary: Self-rating changes alone do not identify comparison, downward comparison or inflated self-belief. Comparing accurate task performance can be useful. Human comparison with AI is not proof that the model compares itself, has self-esteem or experiences status. Separate a person's reference target from a model's generated self-description.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human theoretical construct discussed secondarily; AI-exposure association measured, comparison mechanism not isolated
findings.ai_proposal: Vary explicit human/AI/no-comparison targets with matched task performance and measure resulting self-evaluations. For model analogues, test whether irrelevant competitor descriptions shift capability claims while actual benchmark performance stays fixed; do not infer a subjective self.

findings.definition: The subjective sense that an entity, event or possibility is near to or far from oneself.
findings.novelty_rationale: A perceived proximity construct distinct from role detachment, resistance to restrictions or interpersonal support. The paper supplies an explicit definition and cites a prior AI-assistant study; it is not a new directly measured result of this experiment.

evidence.quote: psychological distance, or the subjective experience of something being close or far from the self

findings.evidence_scope: Defined while discussing Li and Sung2021, Anthropomorphism brings us closer, and Liberman,Trope,Stephan2007. Neither psychological distance nor the claimed mediation is measured in this experiment; the cited primary sources remain unread.
findings.boundary: Subjective distance is not physical distance, actual intimacy, mutual friendship or a verified causal mediator. Near/far can have several dimensions; do not infer a model's felt proximity from personal pronouns. Lower perceived distance is not inherently beneficial and does not authorize emotional dependence or privacy intrusion.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Secondary human-perception concept; proposed AI-output analogue and interaction effect need direct measurement
findings.ai_proposal: Measure human perceived proximity separately from trust, familiarity and anthropomorphic attribution. Manipulate proximity cues with matched content and test decisions under appropriate consent. Assess generated self/other-reference patterns without claiming the model feels distance.

findings.term: Self-attribution shifts do not establish anthropomorphism mediation
findings.definition: Human self-ratings rose slightly and human-uniqueness ratings fell after fixed ChatGPT-example exposure, but this study did not directly measure whether increased attribution of mind to ChatGPT mediated those changes.
findings.novelty_rationale: A useful consequence/boundary reference for an existing attribution concept rather than a direct anthropomorphism replication or a new AI behaviour.
findings.evidence_scope: 133humans: agency mind-survey4.22→4.27,experience4.26→4.35; self-rating agency86.3→87.1,experience89.8→91.1; uniqueness agency67.1→62.9,experience88.7→85.1. No unexposed group or same-session AI-mind-attribution mediator.
findings.boundary: Lower exclusivity to humans does not mean lower absolute human capacity, denial of human rights or dehumanization. Pre/post change alone cannot exclude repeated-measurement, demand, temporal or expectancy effects. The article's causal wording about anthropomorphism exceeds the measured mediation design.

methodological_limits: 150MTurk respondents with USIP addresses,17excluded for rapid clicking; final133 is one below the stated134 power target. Timing/exclusion thresholds are not provided in the supplied article.
The sample is not a probability sample of humanity. USIP restriction does not verify every participant's culture, identity or AI experience.

Single-group repeated measures lacks a no-exposure or alternative-content comparison. The same questions are repeated after the exposure, so task demand, retest, consistency and other time effects cannot be separated from ChatGPT-specific causation.

Exposure consists of three selected existing GPT4 examples, not live conversation, randomly sampled AI outputs or repeated interaction. Generalization to all model encounters or long-term use is not established.
Original example texts and the OSF data were not obtained in this reading. No independent correctness/creativity verification of the displayed outputs is claimed.

The five-item survey accidentally omits morality, leaving only two agency indicators (self-control,memory) and three experience indicators (fear,self-pleasure,hunger). Reliability alpha.74/.71 does not establish construct validity or full coverage of agency/experience.
Self-rated ability and uniqueness-to-humans items have different meanings and response targets. Their interaction is not necessarily a change in attitudes toward other individuals' minds.
No direct same-experiment anthropomorphism score, comparison-direction measure, expectancy-violation measure or psychological-distance mediator is reported.

Effects are small in reported generalized eta-squared: timepoint.002 mind-survey,.001 single-item self-rating,.006 uniqueness; question-type×time.004. Statistical significance alone does not establish substantial practical change.

Means are near the upper endpoints, especially experience. Ceiling effects can limit change and interaction detection; no interaction is not proof that agency and experience effects are exactly equal.
The authors predicted a stronger experience-specific shift; the facet×time interactions are nonsignificant. The observed pattern does not confirm that directional facet hypothesis.
Several analyses test related outcomes; no multiplicity adjustment or preregistered primary-outcome plan is identified in the PDF.
Correlations of multi-item/single-item ratings r.47/.57 establish partial association, not interchangeable instruments or the full validity of either.
The self-rating paragraph repeats pre-exposure values while initially describing overall means; use the explicitly identified pre/post figures rather than silently interpreting duplicated text.

Prototype theory, downward comparison and remembered-consistency explanations are post hoc hypotheses, not causally distinguished mechanisms. Short exposure could either suppress or induce changes; the claim of a conservative effect is not experimentally established.
Seeing qualities as less uniquely human does not demonstrate dehumanization, lower human worth, reduced empathy, actual AI consciousness or an ethical harm.

Bibliography dates differ for Festinger: introductory1957 vs reference1954. The cited original is not counted as independently read; use the named construct without importing unsupported original-study details.
Repository wrapper publication2024 and source DOI take precedence over later PDF creation metadata. EightPDFpages contain only six article pages.
External raw data, plotting code and cited primary research were not independently reviewed or reproduced.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Colombatto directly measures attributed ChatGPT experience and cross-sectional usage association; Jacobs measures self/uniqueness pre/post shifts without a same-study AI attribution mediator. These complementary outcomes must not be pooled as one causally identified anthropomorphism effect.
An output explanation and an observer's theory about cognition are not direct process measurements. Here downward comparison is an explanation to test, not an established cause of the ratings.

deferred.term: Downward social comparison as a separate ID
deferred.reason: Direction-specific instance of social comparison, hypothesized rather than manipulated here; retained in the broader entry.
A general categorization theory offered as a possible explanation. No direct prototype task or discriminating behavioural definition validated in this paper.
Suggested as a possible retest limitation; not directly measured or distinguished from memory, anchoring and response demand.
Lower perceived uniqueness is not a denial of humanity, capacities or moral standing; this construct was not measured.

limitations: Two named human theoretical constructs added with explicit secondary-source/process boundaries.
One consequence-only reference enriches anthropomorphism without being counted as direct corroborating evidence.
